title: Leaving Paris at the war's start and pianist Una Mae Carlisle
summary: He stayed in Paris 14 years and 9 months, was sent home by the American consul, and sailed with Una Mae Carlisle.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: How long did you stay in Paris then? Did you make several trips there or just stay there all those years?
I made trips back, but my trips back was visits here. I just stayed in Paris 14 years and 9 months. You came back when the war started? Oh, yeah, they'd run everybody back.

The American Council. Said for every American throughout Europe, the different councils of the different countries, and they told you what port and the date to be there to catch your boat back to America. And we went to, caught my boat, Unamay Carlisle. She's a great pianist. Oh, yeah. American. And we went to, had to go to Ireland to pick up some Americans. Some Americans were assigned to the same boat that we were assigned to in France. They went to Cove, every other town.

Yeah, Cove, Ireland. And when the boat left Ireland with these Americans, Unamay Carlisle was left. So when the boat pulled out about 30 or 40 feet out in the water, well, they heard a lot of yelling and going on. And they looked back, and that was a wave. So this guy reversed and backed up there together. I told her, gee, you're popular. She was a good entertainer.
Good looking girl too, wasn't she?
Yes. But a great pianist. She was a musician she was. She didn't play like we did. Yes, I'm picking up, she would buy all that music and play it. Could play it.
